followUpTask.name: Flight API reconnection
rootCause: The HTTPS flight import route was not mounted.
The import controller referenced missing flight-cache service exports.
FLIGHT_IMPORT_SECRET was absent from environment wiring, leaving the import guard unusable.
followUpTask.requiredProductionAction: Deploy the updated backend, set the same strong FLIGHT_IMPORT_SECRET on FlySOS and the flight-data server, then schedule pushFlightsToFlySOS.mjs every five minutes.

architectureDecisions: Keep the existing prebuilt frontend asset pair and repair the backend contract rather than rebuilding unavailable frontend source.
Use passengerRightsUrl as the public/API name and rightsDocumentUrl as the canonical AppSetting storage column.
Store new CMS media under the CMS subdirectory and keep claim uploads outside public static serving.
Allow generic PDF MIME values only with a PDF extension and verify the uploaded PDF signature before persistence.
Reuse the existing HTTPS flight push architecture and MySQL flight-cache tables, with a shared advisory lock for pull and push synchronization.
Keep the larger request-body bound scoped to the flight import route and preserve the 1 MB limit for unrelated JSON APIs.
assumptions: The configured MySQL database is available to deployment and can run the idempotent legal-document migration.
Existing root-level CmsMedia filenames are generated server-side and can be safely resolved through the legacy allow-list route.
The active browser bundles in the repository are the deployed frontend assets.
risks: No MySQL server or production credentials are available for live migration/API verification in this workspace.
Actual external deployment was not authorized or performed.
The live flight cache will remain stale until the updated backend and the provider-side five-minute push job are deployed and configured.
reworkHistory: The first regression run failed on the missing passenger-rights schema/controller/public/upload-serving contract; the implementation repaired those root causes before downstream validation.
The historical broad public uploads mount was replaced with CMS-scoped static serving and a legacy CMS allow-list to preserve compatibility without exposing claim files.
Credential-like values in the tracked local environment example were replaced with safe placeholders during the security review.
The flight API follow-up restored the missing HTTPS import route/service contract and documented production deployment as pending.
